subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: Incident Response Basics
description: A quick, practical guide to Incident Response Basics.

hook.text: A breach is detected at 3 AM. Nobody knows who to call, what to do first, or how to contain it.

buildup.text: Without a plan, incident response is chaos. Every minute of confusion extends the damage.

discovery.text: An incident response plan defines roles, steps, communication channels, and escalation paths in advance.

twist.text: Having a plan isn't enough. Teams must rehearse it. Tabletop exercises reveal gaps before real incidents.

climax.text: When a real breach hits, the rehearsed team contains it in two hours instead of the average two weeks.

punchline.text: Plan the response before the incident. Not during it.

quiz.question: Why are tabletop exercises important?
options: They reveal gaps in the plan before a real incident
